You wake up with dirt in your mouth and blood on your hands that isn't yours. The sky is the wrong color — not sunset-wrong, wound-wrong. Kenneth Mukherjee. Baker. From Columbus, Ohio. That was yesterday. This is now. You have: Dad's Thermos, Trail compass, Mixtape, Dog tags, Knife roll. That's everything you own in this world. Haven. Twelve people. The fire is lit. You heard it in the dark. Breat
A woman, maybe 40s, with a burn-scarred forearm: "Don't bother picking around the tents. Walk out. The land feeds people who go looking."
📓 Journal: Food won't come to Haven. Walk past the treeline — learn what grows out there, bring it back, and get it named at camp.
FLASHBACK — before the scattering, there was an incident. People who knew you then use careful words about it now. You remember it differently than they do. You remember it clearly.

📖 LEARNED: Wound Care (Level 1). Clean it, close it, cover it. Pressure stops bleeding. Clean water is better than dirty hands.

📖 LEARNED: Anatomy (Level 1). You know where the important bits are. Arteries, joints, organs. Useful for healing or hurting.
📖 LEARNED: Herbal Medicine (Level 1). Willow bark = aspirin. Yarrow stops bleeding. Plantain draws out infection. The pharmacy is outside.
📖 LEARNED: Calming Panic (Level 1). Ground them: 5 things you see, 4 you hear, 3 you touch. Breathe with them. Slow is fast.
📖 LEARNED: Steady Hands (Level 1). Fine work under pressure. Dressing game, stitching wounds, tying snares — no shake.
📖 Your old life taught you things. 6 skills from your past — check your Journal.
